To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Qkf gene expression correlates strongly with stem cell properties and that Qkf expression decreases with increasing differentiation of neural stem cells.
querkopf is expressed by a subset of adult NSCs and its expression correlates with the self-renewal potential of adult NSCs.

the Qkf promoter is active in a small subset (10%) of cells in the adult subventricular zone and that Qkf promoter activity is strongly correlated with the multipotency and the self-renewal of neural stem cells in the adult mouse subventricular zone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
adult neurogenesis in the subventricle of the brain, a process that has been shown to be involved in the formation of new neurons in the olfactory bulb.
the identification and characterization of a novel marker that may be used to isolate NSCs and to understand the molecular mechanisms regulating NSC self-replication.
the identification of factors regulating the self-renewal of neural stem cells (adult neural stem cells, NSCs) in the adult brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Qkf is a key marker for adult neural stem cells in the SVZ, and its activity decreases as cells progress along the neurogenic lineage.
the highest Qkf promoter activity is associated with the most multipotent and self-renewing cells within the neurogenic subependymal zone.
the Qkf gene is a key marker for adult neural stem cells in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Qkf is a key marker for adult NSC and multipotency in vivo.
Qkf is a key marker for adult neural stem cells and that the Qkf gene expression is regulated by the self-renewal gene Bmi1.
QKF is a key marker for adult NSCs in vivo and that its expression is progressively lost in cells as they become lineage-committed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Qkf expression levels can be used to identify and isolate NSCs in the mouse SVZ in vivo and in vitro.
Querkopf (also known as MYST-4, KAT6b, and MORF) gene expression levels are a marker of neural stem cell (NSC) self-renewal.
the expression of the Qkf gene is strongly correlated with the self-renewal potential of adult neural stem/progenitor cells in the SVZ.
